<!--
The rules are in docs/practices/writing-an-issue.md.

Label it once it exists: capability, step, spike, idea or surface. The shape
below is the same for all five, because what an implementer needs does not
change with why the work was scheduled.

The one rule that matters: the paragraph below has no heading and comes first.
-->

Two or three sentences, no heading, before anything else. What a person cannot
do today, and what they do instead. Not the design, not the drawing, not the
frame number.

## What is missing

What exists, what does not, and where the two meet. A table of piece-and-where-
it-is beats a paragraph. This is where the design reference, the file paths and
the mechanism go.

## In

What has to be built, and **what already exists that it builds on**. Name the
file and the line, and the precedent to follow rather than re-derive.

## Watch for

The wrong build. Name the tempting shortcut and why it is wrong, and the
adjacent thing that should not be widened into.

## Definition of done

One sentence, checkable, in the present tense as a person experiences it.

## How this was found

Optional, and last. Where it was drawn, the session that raised it, the branch
that was abandoned and what it established.
